links.reason: Kural 529 is about estranged kin (தமராகித் தற்றுறந்தார்) returning once the cause of discord is gone; Pazhamozhi 351 is about kin who seem never to help (செய்யார் எனினும் தமர்செய்வர்) against பிறர். The two meet only on 'kin come back to one', and the contrast drawn between a removed cause and the certainty of rain is the linker's framing more than anything either verse argues.

Thirikadugam 51 line 2 சார்ந்தொழுகிக் கண்ணும் சலவர் சலவரே is exactly the case Pazhamozhi 194 pictures: thieves who show themselves as attached (அடைந்தார்போல் காட்டி) by day and take clothes and food in the sleeping hours. The pair joins the general claim to its concrete sign.
links.text_issue: thirikadugam:51 line 1 தூர்ந்துஒழுகி is obscure; the link rests on line 2, which is clear.

links.reason: Kural 473 blames not knowing one's own strength (உடைத்தம் வலியறியார்); Pazhamozhi 317 grants the men are able (ஆற்றுவாரேனும்) and blames attacking without match (நிகரின்றி மேல்விடுதல் ஏதம்). The shift from absolute to relative strength, and the harm to the striker in கல்லொடு கையெறியுமாறு, are both in the Tamil.

Kural 849 describes the failed lesson (காணாதான் ... கண்டானாம் தான்கண்ட வாறு); Pazhamozhi 94 turns it into a rule, மூர்க்கர்க்கு யாதும் மொழியற்க, and gives the cause: the man keeps what he took up (கொண்டதே கொண்டு விடான்), as cloth that has drunk indigo takes no other colour. Description becomes counsel with a reason.

Pazhamozhi 32 mocks others trying to cover men of wide strength (பாசிமேல் இட்டுக் கரந்து மறைக்கலும் ஆமோ); Naladiyar 105 is about the great fallen through old deeds (மேலை வினைப்பயன்), shrinking to millet size. The meeting point, hiding (மறைக்கல் / தேசுள் அடக்கி), is a word rather than a shared claim, so 'safe from suppression, not from fate' is a construction laid on two verses about different things.

Both say not to beg of the hard (மரம்போல் வலிய மனத்தார் / கரப்பார்), so the core is shared advice. The பள்ளியுள் ஐயம் image adds a reason, but the note and teaches add that the hard man is 'rich', which Pazhamozhi 224 does not say, and the begging-from-renouncers sense of பள்ளி is one reading of the word.

Both use the drum for the leaked secret: Kural 1076 அறைபறை அன்னர் கயவர், Pazhamozhi 178 பறைக்கண் கடிப்பிடு மாறு. Pazhamozhi moves the fault to the chooser who passes over worthy kin (வெள்ளமாண்பெல்லாம் உடைய தமரிருப்ப) and takes the mean man into counsel (மறைக்கண் பிரித்தவரை), a real shift the pair shows.

The echo is real: கற்றொன் றறிந்து கசடற்ற (Pazhamozhi 171 line 3) and அரியகற்று ஆசற்றார் (Kural 503). But the subject of line 3 and the sense of முற்றல் and the proverb மற்றதென் பாற்றேம்பல் நன்று are uncertain, and the 'better to leave the task undone' conclusion rests on one way of dividing those words, so the step needs a generous reading.
links.text_issue: pazhamozhi_nanooru:171 lines 2 and 4 are hard to divide (முற்றலை; மற்றதென் பாற்றேம்பல்).

links.reason: Nanmanikkadigai 60's third gem, நகையாகும் நண்ணார்முன் சேறல், names going before those not one's own as laughable; Pazhamozhi 290 shows it, begging to come inside (அகம்புகுதும் என்றிரக்கும்) from those who cannot bear one's face even outside, like a child crying for the hip from those who would not let it follow on the road. The proverb supplies what makes it absurd.

Acharakkovai 69 lists conduct before the great one (முனியார் துனியார் முகத்தெதிர் நில்லார், and not contradicting even காக்கைவெள் என்னும் எனின்) but gives no reason of danger; Naladiyar 164 is about the inescapable wrath of பெருமை யுடையார், who may be the great in virtue rather than the lord one attends. The claim that the courtesies are 'a defence' is supplied by the pairing, not by the Acharakkovai, and joins two different senses of 'the great'.

Kural 508 speaks of the untested outsider (தேரான் பிறனை); Pazhamozhi 206 refuses the trust of one's goods even to those trusted as eminent or kin (சிறந்தார் தமரென்று தேற்றார்கை வையார), removing the exemption the Kural's பிறன் leaves open, and its proverb இறந்தது பேர்தறிவார் இல் makes the loss final. A real condition added to the couplet.

The same phrase closes both: நல்வினை யார்க்கும் கயிறு (Thirikadugam 23) and தம்மைத்தாம் ஆர்க்குங் கயிறு (Pazhamozhi 371). In one giving and conduct are a rope that ties merit; in the other penance and aram practised falsely (சலமொழுகல்) are a rope that ties the doer, so the image turns on sincerity, as teaches says.

Both make counsellors the ruler's eyes (சூழ்வார்கண் ணாக / சுற்றார் பலரைத்தன் கண்ணாக). Kural 445 asks him to choose them; Pazhamozhi 260 shows the lack in distress (உற்றிடர்ப் பட்ட பொழுதின்கண் தேற்றம்) with the cut-string lute, and adds 'many' (பலரை). The 'keeps his state' gloss on the lute is interpretive but fair to the image.

Kural 879 cuts the thorn tree young (இளைதாக முள்மரம் கொல்க) and Pazhamozhi 308 removes thorn with thorn (முள்ளினால் முட்களையு மாறு), both of the enemy. The contrast of timing against means is real and the Pazhamozhi verse applies it to the enemy's inner enemy (தம்பகைக் குள்வாழ் பகை).

Kural 376 பரியினும் ஆகாவாம் பாலல்ல is the abstract of Pazhamozhi 231's scene: the palmyra guarded all night with shouting (ஏஎய் இரவெல்லாம் காத்தாலும்) whose fruit falls only to those it is to fall to (படற்பாலார் கண்ணே படுமே). The second person, the one it falls to, is in the Tamil and is what the scene adds.

The Venus omen is shared and specific: தென் திசை மருங்கின் வெள்ளி ஓடினும் (Puram 117) against அழல்சென்ற மருங்கின் வெள்ளி ஓடாது (Patitruppattu 13), and the immunity-versus-prevention contrast in teaches is true. But neither poem limits or adds a condition to the other; it is a shared figure used two ways, so same_image fits.

Kural 215's ஊருணி நீர்நிறைந் தற்றே is an image for the wise man's wealth that all draw on; Sirupanchamoolam 62's நீர்அறம் is the gift of water as a charity. Joining them rests on the word 'water' only, and the claim that the verse 'makes the Kural's tank literal' is not something either verse does. The link to the Kural also carries no list_adds.
links.text_issue: sirupanchamoolam:62 line 2 பார்அறம் is uncertain in sense.

links.reason: Kural 1075 makes fear (அச்சமே கீழ்களது ஆசாரம்) what holds the base; Pazhamozhi 97 says they do not care about the great blame on them (பெரும்பழி யேறுவ பேணார்) and its proverb has them eat fearlessly (அஞ்சாதே) in a house of weeping. The pairing marks a limit on the couplet: whatever they fear, blame is not it.

Kural 1051 lays the blame of withholding on the giver (அவர்பழி தம்பழி அன்று); Pazhamozhi 384 gives a case where even the never-refusing man (மறாஅ தவனும்) hides what he has, out of pity for those who will go without (பெறாஅஅன் பேதுறுதல் எண்ணி), so that numbers are what is bad (இரந்தூட்குப் பன்மையோ தீது). That is a true condition on the couplet.

The shared word is real: கோள் in Kural 312 (செய்யாமை மாசற்றார் கோள்) and கோளன்றால் in Pazhamozhi 49, both for not returning harm. But Pazhamozhi 49 speaks of a narrower case, harm from those lacking worth (நீர்த்தகவு இல்லார்), and grounds the rule in the dog image; a narrower case with a different ground does not limit the couplet, so it develops rather than qualifies.

Both are Kapilar giving Pari's daughters: யானே பரிசிலன் மன்னு மந்தணன் ... நினக்கியான் கொடுப்பக் கொண்மதி (200) and யானே தந்தை தோழன் ... அந்தணன், புலவன் ... யான்தர இவரைக் கொண்மதி (201). The shift of the claimed ground to friendship with the father is in the Tamil, though 201 also keeps அந்தணன், which teaches underplays.

Both rank enmity above false friendship: தெளிவிலார் நட்பின் பகைநன்று (Naladiyar 219) and the open enemy (செம்மைப் பகை) set above those who attach without caring (தம்மைப் பரியார் தமரா அடைந்தார்) in Pazhamozhi 298. The ranking is a specific shared claim, the two faults named differ, and the Pazhamozhi's two-world cost (இம்மைப் பழியும் மறுமைக்குப் பாவமும்) is a true addition.

Pazhamozhi 124 says friends take each other whole (முழுமெய்யும் கொள்பவே), and 132 has the faultless take the friend's fault as 'our fault' (எம்தீமை என்றே உணர்பதாம்). Reading the second as the moral consequence of the first is an inference, but a fair one under the same heading, and it shows something neither says alone.

The shared claim is plain: the weak provoking the strong ends badly (ஆற்றுவார்க்கு ஆற்றாதார் இன்னா செயல் / சிறியார் பலசெய்தல் ... நன்றொடு வந்ததொன் றன்று). But the 'futility' that teaches and list_adds add rests on குன்றொடு தேன்கலாம் வெற்ப, which is the address to the hill lord, not the verse's argument; the proverb itself says only that it brings no good.
links.text_issue: pazhamozhi_nanooru:294 line 1 நிற்பாறை is likely corrupt for நிற்பாரை.

links.reason: The same word carries both: வேண்டாமை அன்ன விழுச்செல்வம் (Kural 363) and வேண்டாமை வேண்டிய தெல்லாம் தரும் (Pazhamozhi 273). The Pazhamozhi carries the renouncer's virtue into service at court (ஆண்டகை மன்னரைச் சார்ந்தார்) and the case of hardship (அல்லுறினும்), a real change of domain.

Naladiyar 345 says the base, honoured, still do different deeds (கீழ் செய்யும் கருமங்கள் வேறு படும்), as the dog fed from gold eyes others' leavings; Pazhamozhi 170 puts the base on a task and then sits back (ஆக்குவர் ஆற்ற எமக்கென்றே அமர்ந்திருத்தல்), a cat set to guard fish heads. The employer's second fault is in the Tamil.

Kural 160 ranks those who fast (உண்ணாது நோற்பார்) below those who bear harsh words; Valayapathi 66 calls a vow without forbearance (பொறைமைஇல் நோன்பு) darkness within darkness. Turning a ranking into a dependence is a real and specific step between the two.

Both condemn a bad appointment, but Kural 507's point is the ground of it, fondness (காதன்மை கந்தா), which Pazhamozhi 104 does not touch. What teaches calls the double cost, clearing out the fit (ஊழாயினாரைக் களைந்திட்டு) and planting the kanjirai for the jackfruit, belongs to the Pazhamozhi alone. The pair adds little to it.

They meet on a specific act: முல்லைக்குத் தேரும் (Pazhamozhi 74) is the gift Puram 200 tells as Pari's (புனைகொடி முல்லை ... நெடுந்தேர் கொள்கெனக் கொடுத்த). The Pazhamozhi names no giver, and the note says so, but it judges the act knowing folly (அறிமடமும் சான்றோர்க்கு அணி), which the bardic poem does not.

Pazhamozhi 286 strikes the enmity while young (இளைதாய போழ்தே கதித்துக் களையின்); 287 calls it folly to put off answering those who have already harmed (பின்னலிதும் என்றிருத்தல் பேதைமையே), as the bitten cannot take the fleeing snake's fang. Before and after the first blow, both against delay: the pairing is accurate.

The link joins the truster's தெளிவு in Kural 510 (தேரான் தெளிவும்) to the angry man who never becomes clear (தெளியானைத் தேறல் அரிது) in Pazhamozhi 52. The two words are close, but the Pazhamozhi says to step out of his way (மாறி ஒழுகல்), not that his anger is a test of trust, so 'a usable test' stretches the pairing.

The distinctive word is shared: ஏக்கழுத்து (Acharakkovai 91, item 2, correctly named) and ஏக்கழுத்தஞ் செய்தலும் (Sirupanchamoolam 4). Sirupanchamoolam laughs at it as pretension in one who lacks ground; Acharakkovai blames it everywhere because தம்மின் மூத்த உள. Acharakkovai drops Sirupanchamoolam's condition rather than adding one, so this is a meaningful shared word, not a qualification.

Kural 638 lays the duty of telling good on the one at the king's side (உழையிருந்தான் கூறல் கடன்); Pazhamozhi 259 says the attendants (பக்கத்தார்) take the king's faults, since no doll is unlike its maker (செய்தானை ஒவ்வாத பாவையோ இல்). The consequence gives the duty its sanction; 'the one who stays silent' is a fair inference rather than a word of the verse.

Nearly the same figure: பாம்பொடும் இன்னா ... பிரிவு (Naladiyar 220) and இன்னாதே பேஎயோ டானும் பிரிவு (Pazhamozhi 126). The quatrain draws from it the testing before the bond (பொருட்டக்கார்க் கோடலே வேண்டும்), the Pazhamozhi loyalty after it (கலந்தாரைக் கைவிடுதல் ஒல்லா), so the image argues both ways.

Both close on ஒருவர் பொறையிருவர் நட்பு. Naladiyar 223 has the friend bear great wrongs (இறப்பவே தீய செயினும் ... பொறுத்தல்); Pazhamozhi 132 has the faultless own the friend's fault (எம்தீமை என்றே உணர்பதாம்). The shift from enduring to owning is in the Tamil.

Elathi 15's first item, கண்போல்வார்க் காயாமை, and Pazhamozhi 131's காய்ந்தீயார் are the same restraint. But teaches itself says the Pazhamozhi sets the hardest condition, faults seen with one's own eyes (கண்கண்ட குற்றம் உளவெனினும்), and a verse adding a condition is qualifies, not agrees.

Both are about the distress of இனியார். Naladiyar 369 condemns the heart that does not ease (தணியாத உள்ளம்) at the pain it is told; Pazhamozhi 127 says the remedy is not done by words (மொழியால் முடியா), as dew fills no tank. On the reading that the quatrain asks the heart to be moved, the Pazhamozhi raises the bar to deed.
links.text_issue: pazhamozhi_nanooru:127 lines 2-3 (முனியார் செயினும், துனியால்) are hard to construe.

links.reason: Naladiyar 201 has trouble vanish on seeing kin who ask after one (உசாஅத்தன் கேளிரைக் காணக் கெடும்); Pazhamozhi 350 defines good kin by removing distress through deed (வினைமரபின் மற்றதனை நீக்கும்). The difference is real, but the Pazhamozhi does not set deed against asking, so 'ranks the deed' overstates a contrast the verse does not draw.

Sirupanchamoolam 16 says goodness before the worthless (மாண்பில்லார் முன்னர்) is meat in a dog's mouth, wasted; Pazhamozhi 109 says good done to the graceless base (கண்ணில கயவர்) is plucking a tick from a tiger's face, dangerous. Waste and danger are two distinct costs the pair puts side by side.
links.text_issue: sirupanchamoolam:16 line 3 கோய்வாயிற் கீழுயிர்க்(கு)ஈ துற்று is hard to construe.

links.reason: Kural 959 infers lineage from speech (காட்டும் குலத்தில் பிறந்தார்வாய்ச் சொல்); Pazhamozhi 146 infers the hard-to-read mind from kin colour (குலக்குல வண்ணத்தர் ... புலப்பல வண்ணத்த புள்). Both use land (நிலம் / புலம்), and the reversal of sign and signified is real. The note states the birth-group claim as the text's, not as advice.

Kural 995 says scorn hurts even in jest (நகையுள்ளும் இன்னா திகழ்ச்சி); Pazhamozhi 54 says the hearer takes the unfit jest as abuse (வைதாராக் கொண்டு விடுவர்) and the harm comes back on the jester, like the rat with the lamp (தனக்குநோய் செய்து விடல்). The pair shows the hurt at both ends.

The lists overlap only in part: ஆதுலன் (item 2, correctly named) with ஈடற்றார், இளையான் with இளையர், and possibly உயிரிழந்தான் with இறந்தார். The stranger and the old in Acharakkovai have no match in Elathi, so 'nearly the same' overstates. Teaches itself says the two codes do different things, exempting from ஆசாரம் and owing food, so the type is not agrees.
links.text_issue: acharakkovai:100 உயிரிழந்தான் is uncertain (bereaved or near death); elathi:35 தோன்றார் and இறந்தார் are uncertain.

verses.note: The counsel is for patrons (புரவலர்) and givers; taken as giving from the house rather than the king's court.
Addressed to those who attend on the king (heading மன்னரைச் சேர்ந்தொழுகல்), counted under king as his service.
No count word; the three untouchable days (தீண்டாநாள் முந்நாளும்) and twelve days are periods of a rule, not counted items.
இவ்வனைத்தும் counts without a number; டுவாத்திதிநாள் is taken as one item (உவா திதி நாள்), and ஈரந்தி as one item, both twilights.
The rule is phrased as what not to look at (நோக்கார்), but the five are moral vices with moral fruits (எள்ளப் படுவது, நிரயம்), so domain all and no purity norm.
Etiquette before elders (பெரியார்முன்); line 3 பழியவர் கண்ணுள்ளே நோக்கி யுரை is hard to construe.
The verse names செம்பியன் and the hanging fortress (தூங்கும் எயில்); no further identification is supplied.
Heading வீட்டு நெறி suggests release, but the counsel (இம்மைக்கும் உம்மைக்கும்) is not addressed to renouncers alone; இற்பிறப்பு is mentioned as a lesser good, not as a rule.
குடிப்பிறந்தார் ranks the well-born, even unlearned, above others, a birth-rank claim, so norm caste.
A rule of deference to நான்மறையாளர் as to one's own elders; a varna rule, not bodily ritual, so domain all.
Addressed to one who has lived the household life and is urged to renounce (துறவா உடம்பினான் என்ன பயன்); counted as ascetic counsel.
For those who have joined a king (அரசடைந்தார்), so king's service, though the heading is ஊழ்.
No count word, so items null.
Bodily conduct in the presence of the lord (தலைமகன்); if தலைமகன் is the husband this would be a gender rule, but the verse does not make that plain, so no norm.
